era_benchmark_plan.benchmark_rationale: SPY is the standard broad-market benchmark for a STOCKS-sleeve regime-aware momentum strategy. The thesis explicitly references SPY as the regime filter anchor (SPY > 200-day SMA), making it the natural performance yardstick. The operator accepted SPY as the benchmark default without override.

eras.label: Pre-COVID Bull Market
eras.rationale: A sustained risk-on environment where the SPY 200-day SMA regime filter would be persistently active. Tests whether momentum generates alpha in a clean trending regime rather than merely riding beta.

eras.label: COVID Crash and Recovery
eras.rationale: A severe drawdown followed by a rapid V-shaped recovery. The SPY 200-day SMA filter should trigger a risk-off exit during the crash and a re-entry during recovery. Critical stress test for the regime gate and stop-loss logic.

eras.label: Post-COVID Bull and Meme Era
eras.rationale: A momentum-rich environment with elevated retail participation. Tests whether the strategy captures genuine momentum alpha versus noise-driven returns in a frothy market.

eras.label: Rate-Hike Bear Market
eras.rationale: SPY spent extended periods below its 200-day SMA, so the regime filter should suppress most entries. Tests whether the strategy correctly sits out a prolonged drawdown and avoids large losses.

eras.label: Recovery and AI-Driven Bull
eras.rationale: A strong recovery led by a narrow set of large-cap technology names. Tests whether the dynamic momentum screen captures the leading names or dilutes returns across laggards.

eras.label: Recent Validation Window
eras.rationale: The most recent tape available. Ensures the strategy is still relevant under current market microstructure and is not purely a historical artifact. Kept as a held-out validation window where possible.

trial_ledger_budget.rationale: Sweep dimensions: momentum_lookback (3 values: 20, 63, 126) × stop_loss_pct (4 values: 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20) × regime_filter (2 values: SPY_200SMA, SPY_50SMA) × max_positions (1 anchor: 10) = 24 base variants. Doubling for rebalance_frequency sweep (WEEKLY vs DAILY) yields 48 total variants. With 4 eras (bull-2018, bear-2020, recovery-2020-2022, post-hike-2022-2026) that is 48 × 4 = 192 bench runs. max_bench_runs=192 satisfies the constraint max_total_variants × eras.length = 48 × 4 = 192. Budget is conservative: all signals are OHLCV-derived from alpaca_equity_ohlcv with no external data pulls, so compute cost is negligible and estimated at 0.0 USD pending infrastructure pricing. The 48-variant ceiling keeps the multiple-comparisons correction tractable and avoids over-fitting risk flagged in the known-good momentum template lessons. Server normalization: Server raised the trial-ledger budget to cover 1 variants across 6 eras after sectioned Talon synthesis.

multiple_comparisons_plan.notes: Sweep dimensions: momentum lookback (63-day anchor, default accepted), regime filter (SPY_200SMA, default accepted), stop-loss pct (5%–20% in 5% steps = 4 variants), max positions (10, default accepted), rebalance frequency (WEEKLY, default accepted). The clarification answers collapsed most sweep axes to single values; only the stop-loss sweep remains open with 4 variants across 3 eras = 12 effective bench runs. Bonferroni correction applied: alpha = 0.05 / 12 ≈ 0.004. If the operator later reopens the lookback or position-count sweep, effective_trials_estimate and adjusted_significance_level must be recalculated before promotion.
